title: Pathologic fractures due to any cause
summary: Three pathologic fractures on separate occasions within a 12-month period (see 1.00J), AND impairment-related physical limitation lasting 12+ months with one of: walker/bilateral canes need, one-upper-extremity inability with one-handed device, or both-upper-extremities inability.

children.criterion: Three pathologic fractures occurring on separate, distinct occasions within a 12-month period (see 1.00J)
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning lasting 12+ months AND medical documentation of one of B.1, B.2, or B.3
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, for at least 12 continuous months
One of: B.1 (walker/bilateral canes), B.2 (one upper extremity inability + one-handed device), B.3 (both upper extremities inability)
Documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a walker, bilateral canes, or bilateral crutches (see 1.00C6d), or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of both hands (see 1.00C6e(i))

Inability to use one upper extremity to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4), AND documented medical need for a one-handed, hand-held assistive device requiring the use of the other upper extremity, or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of one hand (see 1.00C6e(ii))
Inability to use both upper extremities to the extent that neither can be used to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4)
